title: Reliable Third-Party Library Detection in Android and its Security Applications
venue: ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
detection_method: 3-layer Merkle tree profiles (Package → Class → Method) with fuzzy descriptors that replace custom types with 'X' placeholders; CHA for hierarchy analysis; similarity score 0-1 for partial matches
module_decoupling: Package-structure-based — libraries are identified by matching pre-built profiles against package subtrees in decompiled DEX
features_used: Method signatures with fuzzy type descriptors
Merkle tree of (Package, Class, Method) layers
matching_algorithm: Profile-based matching using Merkle tree hashing across 3 layers; each layer propagates upward via hash composition; similarity score calculated for partial matches when exact hashes differ
obfuscation_handling: 100% resilient to identifier renaming via fuzzy descriptors (custom types replaced with 'X' placeholder); no protection against package flattening (−75% F1), control-flow randomization, or method inlining
r8_resilience: Version F1 drops to 12.7% on adjacent versions under R8 shrinkage+optimization (Group-1 version F1 64%)
version_level_f1: 97.4% precision at version level; Group-1 version F1 64%, drops to 12.7% under R8
recall: Not explicitly reported (library-level recall embedded in F1 of ~83%)
speed: 82s per app profile generation; 2.8s per library for profile generation
dataset_size: 164 libraries, 2,065 versions; tested on 96,995 packages from 3,590 apps
partial_lib_handling: Score-based (similarity score 0-1); partial matches supported via fuzzy descriptor fallback when exact hash mismatches
sbom_output: Partial — outputs library name and version list, but not in standard SBOM format (no CycloneDX/SPDX)
cve_mapping: No built-in CVE mapping; demonstrated security analysis manually (vulnerability window ~190 days for Facebook SDK; 3.7B device installs affected by crypto API misuse in ad libs)
transitive_deps: No — does not handle transitive dependency resolution
strengths: Fuzzy descriptors are a foundational obfuscation-resilience technique
weaknesses: Fragile against modern R8 transformations (F1 drops to 12.7% under shrinkage+optimization)
No protection against package flattening (−75% F1), control-flow randomization, method inlining
No CDG-based module decoupling — relies on package structure
impact_on_project: Foundational baseline for version-level library detection. The fuzzy descriptor technique (replacing custom types with 'X') is a key obfuscation-resilience mechanism worth adopting, but the reliance on package-structure-based module decoupling is a critical weakness given modern R8 obfuscation. The 3-layer Merkle tree structure provides an elegant profile representation but is insufficient alone. The 12.7% R8 version F1 establishes the gap this project must close. LibScout's approach should serve as a pre-R8 baseline comparator, not the core architecture.
